source_text: Ἐδίδαξε δὲ ἡμᾶς ταῦτα τὸ ἅγιον προφητικὸν πνεῦμα, διὰ Μωϋσέως φῆσαν τῷ πρώτῳ πλασθέντι ἀνθρώπῳ εἰρῆσθαι ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ οὕτως· „Ἰδοὺ πρὸ προσώπου σου τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ τὸ κακόν, ἔκλεξαι τὸ ἀγαθόν“. Καὶ πάλιν διὰ Ἡσαΐου, τοῦ ἑτέρου προφήτου, ὡς ἀπὸ προσώπου τοῦ πατρὸς τῶν ὅλων καὶ δεσπότου θεοῦ εἰς τοῦτο λεχθῆναι οὕτως· „Λούσασθε, καθαροὶ γένεσθε, ἀφέλετε τὰς πονηρίας ἀπὸ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν, μάθετε καλὸν ποιεῖν, κρίνατε ὀρφανῷ καὶ δικαιώσατε χήραν, καὶ δεῦτε καὶ διαλεχθῶμεν, λέγει κύριος· καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν αἱ ἁμαρτίαι ὑμῶν ὡς φοινικοῦν, ὡσεὶ ἔριον λευκανῶ, καὶ ἐὰν ὦσιν ὡς κόκκινον, ὡς χιόνα λευκανῶ. Καὶ ἐὰν θέλητε καὶ εἰσακούσητέ μου, τὰ ἀγαθὰ τῆς γῆς φάγεσθε, ἐὼν δὲ μὴ εἰσακούσητέ μου, μόχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται· τὸ γὰρ στόμα κυρίου ἐλάλησε ταῦτα“. Τὸ δὲ προειρημένον „Μάχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται“ οὐ λέγει διὰ μαχαιρῶν φονενθήσεσθαι τοὺς παρακούσαντας, ἀλλ᾿ ἡ μάχαιρα τοῦ θεοῖ ἐστι τὸ πῦρ. οὗ βορὰ γίνονται οἱ τὰ φαῦλα πράττειν αἱρούμενοι. Διὰ τοῦτο λέγει· „Μάχαιρα ὑμᾶς κατέδεται· τὸ γὰρ στόμα κυρίου ἐλάλησεν“. Εἰ δὲ καὶ περὶ τεμνούσης καὶ αὐτίκα ἀπαλλασσούσης μαχαίρας ἔλεγεν, οὐκ ἂν εἶπε „Κατέδεται“. Ὥστε καὶ Πλάτων εἰπών. „Αἰτία ἑλομένου, θεὸς δ᾿ ἀναίτιος“ παρὰ Μωϋσέως τοῦ προφήτου λαβὼν εἶπε· πρεσβύτερος γὰρ Μωϋσῆς καὶ πάντων τῶν ἐν Ἕλλησι συγγραφέων. Καὶ πάντα. ὅσα περὶ ἀθανασίας ψυχῆς ἢ τιμωριῶν τῶν μετὰ θάνατον ἢ θεωρίας οὐρανίων ἢ τῶν ὁμοίων δογμάτων καὶ φιλόσοφοι καὶ ποιηταὶ ἔφασαν, παρὰ τῶν προφητῶν τὰς ἀφορμὰς λαβόντες καὶ νοῆσαι δεδύνηνται καὶ ἐξηγήσαντο. Ὅθεν παρὰ πᾶσι σπέρματα ἀληθείας δοκεῖ εἶναι· ἐλέγχονται δὲ μὴ ἀκριβῶς νοήσαντες. ὅταν ἐναντία αὐτοὶ ἑαυτοῖς λέγωσιν. Ὥστε ὅ φαμεν, πεπροφητεῦσθαι τὰ μέλλοντα γίνεσθαι, οὐ διὰ τὸ εἱμαρμένης ἀνάγκῃ πράττεσθαι λέγομεν· ἀλλὰ προγνώστου τοῦ θεοῦ ὄντος τῶν μελλόντων ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων πραχθήσεσθαι, καὶ δόγματος ὄντος παρ᾿ αὐτόν κατ᾿ ἀξίαν τῶν πράξεων ἕκαστον ἀμείψεσθαι μέλλοντα τῶν ἀνθρώπων. καὶ τὰ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ κατ᾿ ἀξίαν τῶν πραττομένων ἀπαντήσεσθαι διὰ τοῦ προφητικοῦ πνεύματος προλέγει, εἰς ἐπίστασιν καὶ ἀνάμνησιν ἀεὶ ἄγων τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος, δεικνύς, ὅτι καὶ μέλον ἐστιν αὐτῷ καὶ προνοεῖται αἰτῶν. Κατ᾿ ἐνέργειαν δὲ τῶν φαύλων δαιμόνων θάνατος ὡρίσθη κατὰ τῶν τὰς Ὑστάσπου ἢ Σιβύλλης ἢ τῶν προφητῶν βίβλους ἀναγινωσκόντων, ὅπως διὰ τοῖ φόβου ἀποστρέψωσιν ἐντυγχάνοντας τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῶν καλῶν γνῶσιν λαβεῖν, αἰτοῖς δὲ δουλεύοντας κατέχωσιν· ὅπερ εἰς τέλος οὐκ ἴσχυσαν πρᾶξαι. Ἀφόβως μὲν γὰρ οὐ μόνον ἐντυγχάνομεν αὐταῖς, ἀλλὰ καὶ ὑμῖν, ὡς ὁρᾶτε, εἰς ἐπίσκεψιν φέρομεν, ἐπιστάμενοι πᾶσιν εὐάρεστα φανήσεσθαι· κἂν ὀλίγους δὲ πείσωμεν, τὰ μέγιστα κερδήσαντες ἐσόμεθα· ὡς γεωργοὶ γὰρ ἀγαθοὶ παρὰ τοῖ δεσπόζοντος τὴν ἀμοιβὴν ἕξομεν.
pass_a_gloss: The holy prophetic Spirit taught us these things, saying to the first created man through Moses thus: 'Behold, before your face are the good and the evil, choose the good.' And again, through Isaiah, another prophet, it was said from the face of the Father of all and the Lord God thus: 'Wash, become clean, remove the evil deeds from your souls, learn to do good, judge the orphan and justify the widow, and come and let us reason, says the Lord; and if your sins are like scarlet, I will whiten them like wool, and if they are like crimson, I will whiten them like snow. And if you wish and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the earth, but if you do not listen to me, the sword will devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken these things.' The previously mentioned 'The sword will devour you' does not say that those who disobey will be killed by swords, but the sword of God is fire, of which the food is those who choose to do evil things. Therefore, it says: 'The sword will devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken.' If it were speaking about a cutting and immediately destroying sword, it would not have said 'will devour.' So also Plato, having said 'The cause is he who chooses, and God is without cause,' took this from Moses the prophet, for Moses is older than all the Greek writers. And all the things that philosophers and poets have said about the immortality of the soul or the punishments after death or the contemplation of heavenly things or similar doctrines, they took the starting points from the prophets and were able to understand and explain them. From which it seems that there are seeds of truth among all; but they are convicted of not having understood accurately when they say things contrary to themselves. So what we say, that the things to come were prophesied, we do not say because they are done by necessity of fate; but because God, being foreknowing, knows what will be done by all men, and there is a doctrine with Him to reward each person according to their deeds, and through the prophetic Spirit, He foretells the things that will happen to each person according to their deeds, always bringing the human race to knowledge and remembrance, showing that He cares for them and provides for them. But by the operation of evil demons, death was ordained against those who read the books of Hystaspes or Sibyl or the prophets, so that through fear they might turn away the people who approach them from gaining knowledge of good things, and keep those who serve them in bondage; which they were not able to accomplish in the end. For we approach them fearlessly, and we bring them to you, as you see, for examination, knowing that they will appear pleasing to all; and even if we persuade a few, we will have gained the greatest things; for as good farmers, we will have the reward from the Master.

pass_b_english: The holy prophetic Spirit taught us these things, declaring through Moses to the first man created by God: "Behold, before you lie the good and the evil; choose the good." Again, through Isaiah, another prophet, the word came from the Father of all and the Master, God, saying: "Wash yourselves, become clean, remove your evil deeds from my sight; learn to do good, seek justice, defend the orphan, plead for the widow. Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be white as wool; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like snow. If you are willing and obedient, you shall eat the good of the land; but if you refuse and rebel, the sword shall devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken" (Isaiah 1:16-20). The earlier statement "the sword shall devour you" does not mean that the disobedient will be killed by physical swords; rather, the sword of God is fire, and its fuel is those who choose to do evil. Therefore it says: "The sword shall devour you; for the mouth of the Lord has spoken." If it were speaking of a sword that cuts and destroys at once, it would not have said "devour." So also Plato, when he said, "The cause lies with the one who chooses; God is blameless," took this from Moses the prophet, for Moses is older than all the writers among the Greeks. And all that philosophers and poets have said about the immortality of the soul, or punishments after death, or the contemplation of heavenly things, or similar doctrines—they received their starting points from the prophets, and were able to understand and explain them. Hence there appear to be seeds of truth among all people; yet they are convicted of not having understood accurately whenever they contradict themselves. When we say that future events were prophesied, we do not say this because they happen by the necessity of fate; but because God is foreknowing, knowing what all human beings will do, and because there is a decree with Him to repay each person according to their deeds. Through the prophetic Spirit He foretells what will befall each according to their works, ever leading the human race to knowledge and remembrance, showing that He cares for them and provides for them. By the operation of evil demons, death was appointed against those who read the books of Hystaspes, or the Sibyl, or the prophets, so that through fear they might turn away from the knowledge of good things those who approach these writings, and hold in bondage those who serve the demons; yet they were not able to accomplish this in the end. For we approach these writings without fear, and we bring them to you, as you see, for examination, knowing they will prove pleasing to all; and even if we persuade only a few, we shall have gained the greatest things, for as good farmers we shall receive the reward from the Master.
